domain_label: Pre-made / AI-generated / Shareable Catalog Model & the Single-vs-Multi-User Owner Decision
purpose: A method for turning the KB2 tree into 'choose-what-to-study' catalog OBJECTS: pre-made blueprint-aligned defaults, AI-generated goal->tree+ordering proposals, and shareable exportable/importable catalogs — every catalog node traceable to a KB1 blueprint or sibling content node with its provenance tags inherited, every AI proposal provenance-stamped and owner-gated (propose-not-commit, mirroring kgverify), and all sharing shipped as reversible, single-user-safe import/export files BEHIND the catalog_multiuser owner escalation which curric frames but never decides; curric composes dental/toefl/contenteng by reference and defers sequencing to sched and progress rollup to engage.
assumptions: a catalog is an ordered, faceted SELECTION over the KB2 tree; this KB owns the catalog object and sharing model, not the tree (KB2) or the blueprints (KB1)
every catalog node traces to a KB1 blueprint node or a sibling-produced content node and inherits its [FACT-source]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tags; no node is invented outside this trace
AI-generated catalogs are proposals composed from grounded sources, provenance-stamped and owner-gated, never auto-committed (mirroring kgverify's propose-not-commit)
catalog sharing ships as reversible, single-user-safe import/export files so nothing pre-commits the app to a multi-user architecture
the single-user-vs-multi-user question is an OWNER decision (decisions_pending.catalog_multiuser) that curric frames with both models and their consequences and NEVER resolves inside the specialist
exclusions: resolving the single-user-vs-multi-user model choice (owner decision; curric frames and escalates only)
the prerequisite/adaptive sequencing logic that computes a catalog's order (sched+learner)
the progress/mastery rollup and gamification a catalog displays (engage+uxguide)
the studiable content inside catalog items and its decomposition (contenteng)
the tree information architecture (KB2) and the exam blueprints themselves (KB1)

glossary.definition: An ordered 'choose-what-to-study' SELECTION over the KB2 tree — a set of tree nodes plus a per-item order and facet filters (pathology/physiology/everything) — existing in three kinds: pre-made, AI-generated, and shareable. Every node traces to a KB1 blueprint or sibling content node. [FACT — KB scope]

A curated, blueprint-aligned DEFAULT catalog shipped with the app, source-traced to KB1 and coverage-structured where weights are [UNKNOWN]; illustrative examples: 'INBDE full-coverage', 'Step 1 Pathology-only', 'TOEFL Reading ladder'. [FACT — model; examples illustrative]

A learner GOAL turned into a proposed tree + ordering COMPOSED from KB1 blueprints + contenteng content + sched sequencing; the AI arranges grounded nodes and invents nothing. It is provenance-stamped and owner-gated (propose-not-commit), never auto-committed. [FACT — model]

The honesty tag + source trace attached to every AI-generated (and shared) catalog, recording which KB1/contenteng/sched nodes it was composed from and carrying forward each origin's [FACT-source]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag so no estimate is laundered into a fact. [FACT — discipline]

The rule that an AI-generated catalog is PROPOSED and the owner/approval-flow must accept before it becomes a committed default or shared object — mirroring kgverify's 'propose, never silently rewrite'; an ungated or unstamped ship is a flag condition. [FACT — discipline]

A catalog modeled as an exportable/importable, provenance-stamped FILE so another learner can reuse the structure; grounded in the Osmosis shareable-playlist pattern and shipped as reversible import/export BEHIND the multi-user escalation. [FACT — model]

The design stance that catalog sharing is implemented as export/import/remove of files WITHOUT a multi-user architecture and can be added or withdrawn with no schema lock-in, keeping the app's single-user baseline intact and the owner's multi-user decision fully open. [FACT — design stance]

The central collision between the shareable-catalog feature and the single-user architecture baked into nearly every specialist: model A (single-user with importable/exportable files: files, provenance, no accounts) versus model B (multi-user accounts: identity, permissions, moderation, attribution). [FACT — the framed tension]

The named OWNER-DECISION escalation: any request requiring resolution of single-user-with-files vs multi-user accounts escalates to human_review / owner_decision; curric presents both models and their consequences and STOPS, never deciding. [FACT — escalation contract]

The remit rule that curric composes dental's INBDE blueprint, toefl's TOEFL structure and contenteng's content by REFERENCE into catalogs, and hands sequencing to sched and progress rollup to engage, re-authoring no sibling's blueprint, coaching, content, order or progress. [FACT — remit boundary]

A catalog can therefore be audited back to grounded, source-traced structure, and it inherits the [FACT-source]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tags of its blueprint origins. No catalog may contain a node invented outside this trace. [FACT — invariant]

nodes.definition: The purpose of the shareable model: 'someone learning something else can reuse the STRUCTURE'. A shared catalog exports the ARRANGEMENT (the selection, ordering surface and facets) so a different learner — even one on a different exam or goal — can import and adapt it. What travels is the traceable structure and its provenance stamp, not the other learner's progress or private state. Reuse is why sharing exists; it is delivered by the reversible file model behind the owner escalation. [FACT — model rationale]

structure + provenance travel; progress/private state do not

nodes.definition: The consequence map curric presents (without choosing): Model A (single-user with importable/exportable files) => simple, reversible, provenance-carrying, no identity/permissions/moderation, no cross-user attribution or shared library. Model B (multi-user accounts) => identity, permissions, moderation, attribution, a shared library and richer reuse, but accounts, privacy obligations, and irreversible schema commitment. Curric lays these out so the owner can decide; it asserts no preference. [FACT — decision framing]

This closes the curric remit: it owns the shelf, the selectors and the sharing mechanism, not the goods, the sequencing, the progress, or the multi-user decision. [FACT — synthesis]

priority_rationale: The catalog object frame and traceability invariant come first because every catalog kind inherits the ordered-selection model and the source-trace requirement; the multi-user tension, the never-decide discipline and the named catalog_multiuser owner escalation come next because they are the central binding boundary the whole sharing model is designed behind; the AI-generation provenance stamp and owner gate, the reversible file sharing, and the pre-made defaults then define the three kinds; the compose/defer boundaries fix what curric never re-authors; and the synthesis closes the KB as the complete, gated, traceable catalog model.

dominance_rules.rule: The owner gate dominates AI auto-commit
